title: Prefetch affinity + fragmentation reuse pool with late-binding kernel matching
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Problem: Paged attention workloads exhibit frequent small allocations in the KV cache as many short-lived contexts are interleaved with long-lived sessions. The current allocator creates fragmentation and forces early eviction of useful segments, increasing prefill work and tail latency. Additionally, the runtime currently selects kernels at request enqueue time based on coarse heuristics; under paged attention and varying sequence distributions this leads to suboptimal kernel choices and costly handoffs during decode.

Goal: Implement a prefetch-affinity allocator + reusable fragment pool and a late-binding kernel-matching pass in the scheduler so we can 1) reduce KV fragmentation and re-alloc churn, 2) increase fragment reuse for short-lived contexts, and 3) pick kernels that better match prefilling + decode patterns to reduce decode stalls and cross-kernel handoffs. Target measurable improvements in tail p95/p99 decode latency and reduction of prefill bytes per request for paged attention workloads.

Scope: Design and implement these components in the runtime: the affinity-based prefill planner, a soft-reserve reusable fragment pool with aging buckets, eviction watermark updates to support reuse, and a late-binding kernel matcher that runs just before batch dispatch and is aware of allocated fragment shapes and prefill plans. Add unit tests, integration tests, synthetic benchmarks (seq-dist and interleaving workloads), and update observability metrics (fragmentation ratio, reuse hits, kernel handoff count).
acceptance_criteria: Integration: runtime builds and passes existing CI + new integration tests for paged attention fragment reuse
Performance: synthetic interleaving workload shows >= 20% reduction in average prefill bytes and >= 10% improvement in p95 decode latency vs baseline
Correctness: no regression on existing KV eviction invariants; can reproduce and validate reuse hit metrics in staging
Observability: new metrics emitted: fragment_reuse_hits, fragment_eviction_watermark, kernel_handoff_count, prefill_bytes_per_request
Safety: feature gated behind config flag 'prefetch_affinity_v1' and rollout plan documented in runtime-1.22 release notes
discussion: 2026-02-12 Aisha Chen: Kickoff — initial design doc linked (https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNT/Prefetch+Affinity+and+Reusable+Fragment+Pool). Proposing soft-reserve pool with 3 aging buckets (hot/medium/cold) and a per-tenant quota to avoid noisy tenants starving the pool.

2026-02-15 Marco Alvarez: POC allocator sketch committed to branch feat/prefetch-affinity. Local microbench shows decreased allocator churn but increased synchronous locking under high concurrency; need to explore per-shard lock striping.

2026-02-20 Riley Park (reviewer): Review feedback — prefer lock-free freelists for hot bucket; recommend deferring global compaction to an async background pass to avoid prefill stalls. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2856

2026-02-25 Nadia Singh (Scheduler): Kernel late-binding idea looks good; we need scheduler hooks to expose actual allocated fragment shapes to the matcher. Added dependency on scheduler API change (ENG-73300, placeholder).

2026-03-02 Marco Alvarez: Implemented late-binding matcher prototype. Uses a lightweight cost model (memory layout + expected decode length) to pick kernel variant. Unit tests added. Example benchmark (seq-dist-imbalanced) attached: https://dashboards.redwood.com/bench/runtime/prefetch-affinity/proto-2026-03-02

2026-03-05 Performance team (bench): Observed 12% p95 improvement but p99 unchanged under heavy multi-tenant noise. Hypothesis: eviction watermark configuration too aggressive; experiment with raising soft-reserve for hot bucket.
2026-03-09 Marco Alvarez: Added adaptive watermark adjustment that increases hot-bucket soft-reserve when reuse_hit_rate > 0.35. Running long-run repros in staging.

2026-03-11 Ops: Staging soak for 72h completed. Fragmentation ratio decreased from 0.34 -> 0.18 on synthetic interleaving workload. No increased OOM events observed. Preparing rollout plan and console feature-flag UI (linked: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNT/Prefetch+Affinity+Rollout+Plan)
2026-03-12 Security: quick review — no new network/TLS concerns. KMS/HSM unaffected. Marking security_review_required=false for this change.
